title: Surviving AI
subtitle: The Promise and Peril of Artificial Intelligence
pitch: A short, clear walk from today's narrow AI to general AI and superintelligence, and why making it friendly is the key problem of the century.

chapters.t: AI in the past and present
chapters.g: A quick history of AI and what it can do now.
Near term advances, such as self driving cars and smart assistants.

chapters.t: From digital disruption to economic singularity
chapters.g: What happens if machines can do most jobs.
Arguments for and against general AI being possible.

chapters.t: When might the first AGI arrive?
chapters.g: Expert surveys and the difficulty of timing.
How a general AI might improve itself quickly.
Why a superintelligence could be very good or very bad.

chapters.t: Can we ensure that superintelligence is "friendly"?
chapters.g: Approaches to friendly AI, from control to value loading.
Why we should act now, while there is time.

ideas: AI goes from narrow to general to super.
General AI could improve itself fast.
Friendly AI is the central challenge.
An economic singularity could arrive before a technological one.

args.a: Superintelligence could arrive this century and must be made friendly.
args.c: Skeptics argue the jump from narrow to general AI is much harder than it looks.

args.a: We should start working on friendliness now.
args.c: Some say we cannot solve safety for systems we have not built yet.

questions: Which step, narrow to general or general to super, worries you more?
What would a friendly superintelligence do on its first day?
Is an economic singularity already starting?

quiz.q: What do ANI, AGI and ASI stand for?
quiz.w: The book is built on these stages.
AI that is good for humans.

o: When machines can do most jobs
quiz.w: Chace coined the phrase for mass automation.
